anchor_comparisons.concrete_comparison: The approved L1 task is a static 5x5x3 isometric pile: the agent rotates views and clicks frontmost ray-visible blockers and diamonds, while the UI exposes pick durability, inventory, hazards, and procedure. Ballast Lantern adds autonomous target motion, a momentum-bearing cage, binary control timing, and a coupled second target, so even its broadest profile is above this static spatial-control anchor.

anchor_comparisons.concrete_comparison: The approved L3 task is a 2D inertial ball with three ordered lamps, three walls, three wells, and a final cup. Its screenshot exposes the ball, obstacles, current lamp counter, and recovery counters, while full interaction is continuous analog dragging. Ballast Lantern has less 2D topology and only one binary channel, but its baseline combines hidden drift-law inference with a specimen/crate resource allocation and a narrow vertical capture window. That makes L4 plausible relative to this L3 anchor, while the control demands are not identical.

anchor_comparisons.concrete_comparison: The approved L5 task visibly presents a 5x5 changing board, an exact target score, current score, move budget, cascade receipt, refill preview, and forbidden licorice. Each accepted adjacent swap changes the board and refill cursor, so four decisions are state-dependent and must hit an exact total. Ballast Lantern has stronger temporal/motor demands but only a one-dimensional binary control and no comparable visible combinatorial ledger; its L4 baseline should not be promoted to L5 from parameter size alone.

visible_baseline_solution: A normal screenshot-only solution must read the instruction and track the luminous specimen, the inertial cage, the wake, depth labels, and the crate after it appears. In full mode it holds Space to engage HAUL and releases Space for COAST; in simplified mode it clicks persistent HAUL or COAST buttons. It must infer specimen direction and likely law from successive frames, anticipate cage velocity rather than chase the current center, keep the specimen within the cage often enough to avoid draining its capture reserve, then move the same cage to the spawned crate and hold overlap long enough to fill the crate before allowing the specimen to reach its terminal threshold. A missed overlap can drain the specimen meter; zero capture escapes, capture completion with an unfinished crate becomes specimen_only, and the run only passes when both meters are complete. The cage and target positions and inside glow are visible, but no numeric capture or crate progress is rendered, so the agent must estimate allocation from visible overlap, motion, its action history, and the task's terminal feedback.

baseline_judgment.rationale: The current L4/full assignment is source-supported as the first built configuration: the baseline uses all four drift laws, no trend beacon, a three-sample wake, a narrow inertial cage, faster motion, tight capture economics, and a late competing crate. It is materially above the approved static L1 voxel task, and its hidden-law plus resource-allocation problem is plausibly above the approved L3 Gyroscopic Tilt Board despite the latter's richer 2D topology and analog control. The approved L5 Exact-Change Candy Cascade has four state-changing combinatorial swaps with a visible score/receipt ledger, so Ballast Lantern should remain below or at most comparable to that high anchor. The source supports a relative ordering of the five profiles, not calibrated absolute completion rates. The generator's reference schedule, exclusive-crate-fill threshold, and event-count filter certify generated worlds only; they are not run-time action quotas in the grader.

findings.claim: The capture and crate progress meters are central to the success condition and are replayed by grading, but no numeric meter, progress bar, or intermediate allocation readout is rendered in the normal task UI.
findings.causal_explanation: The generator updates capture_meter and crate_meter on every overlap tick and turns capture completion with an unfinished crate into specimen_only. The browser renders positions, wake dots, inside styling, and terminal PASS/FAIL, but its markup has no meter elements or values. A screenshot-only agent can observe whether it is currently overlapping a target, yet cannot directly observe how much crate service remains or how close the specimen is to the terminal threshold. This makes the resource-allocation burden and the large cross-profile changes in hidden rates materially less observable than the instructions claim.

evidence.explanation: Overlap updates both meters, zero capture escapes, and capture completion is secured only if the crate meter is already complete.

The independent grader reads the replayed meter values and reports them only after terminal grading.
The frontend test explicitly forbids ballast meter/readout/tick/velocity tokens, corroborating that this omission is part of the shipped UI contract.

findings.recommended_action: Before treating the allocation profiles as calibrated screenshot-only tasks, expose bounded progress for both meters or redesign the goal around visible progress; preserve the same underlying world and replay contract while validating human and agent solvability.

concise_summary: Keep the current L4/full source assignment and the relative D1 < D2 < D3 < D4 <= D5 profile ordering. The profiles change active prediction, precision, motion-history, and coupled allocation demands, and the two interaction modes are source-equivalent apart from input surface and grading identity. Record the missing visible meter progress as a major screenshot-only fairness limitation and the inert D1/D2 darter intervals as a minor unused-parameter issue; no historical preservation claim or empirical calibration is available.
limitations: This was source-only review. No browser, task materialization, grader replay, independent verifier, human play, VNC calibration, or computer-use-agent measurement was run.
The source contains no historical pre-control Ballast Lantern implementation, so preservation is limited to current default versus explicit D4/full comparison.

The hidden meter gap may make the source-level difficulty ordering overstate what a normal screenshot-only agent can observe.
